premium_projects.subcategory: Climate Change Mitigation/Adaptation (Clean Energy, Agroforestry etc.)
premium_projects.name: REFORESTACION
premium_projects.action: Sowing Life reforestation program, which consists of providing economically for the planting in a nursery and permanent place of plants in the basins, sub-basins and deforested areas of the Province of El Oro, together with other organizations and the Prefecture of El Oro. Together, 150,000 trees of their own species are planted in the planting areas to be replanted.
premium_projects.challenge: Every year the natural forests in the uplands of the province where the water sources are born are reduced, which has caused the decline of the most important resource on the planet, water, year after year. During the months of October and November of each year, there is a reduction in the water in the rivers that supply drinking and irrigation water in the province, mainly causing a shortage of water for irrigation, which is why it is necessary to contribute to the reforestation of the basins and subbasins and deforested areas of our province. We also ensure a supply of natural nutrients from these future forests and the capture of 3.5 metric tons per tree and per year of carbon dioxide when the trees are 20 years old.
premium_projects.intended_outcome: reforestation of basins, sub-basins of the rivers that supply water to the province, reforestation of deforested areas, to guarantee in a certain way in the future the supply of water for human consumption and irrigation, and the capture of carbon dioxide to produce pure oxygen, this as a measure of adaptation and mitigation of climate change.

premium_projects.source: FTUSA Premium project (sample data, own record) PROJ-C603F046
premium_projects.name: IRON SHEETS LOAN PROJECT
premium_projects.action: The Iron Sheets Loan Project is designed to support workers in improving their housing conditions by providing affordable loans to purchase iron sheets (roofing materials). Through this initiative workers will access quality roofing materials and repay the cost in manageable installments over an agreed period. The project aims to promote safe durable and decent housing while reducing the financial burden of making large upfront payments. It also contributes to workers’ welfare dignity and long-term socio-economic stability.
premium_projects.challenge: Many workers live in inadequate housing due to low incomes making it difficult to afford durable roofing materials. As a result they face poor living conditions health risks and limited access to financing for home improvements compounded by low savings capacity.
premium_projects.intended_outcome: Improved access to durable roofing will enhance workers’ living conditions dignity and overall well-being. It is expected to improve health outcomes boost morale and job satisfaction and reduce stress linked to poor housing. The loan scheme also promotes financial inclusion through affordable repayment plans while enabling long-term asset building for workers and their families ultimately contributing to higher productivity at work.

These stoves are energy-efficient cost-effective and environmentally friendly compared to traditional cooking methods.The loan scheme will enable workers to acquire the stoves through affordable manageable installments paid over an agreed period. premium_projects.source: FTUSA Premium project (sample data, own record) PROJ-D00ABA8E
premium_projects.name: TEA PLANTATION MAINTENANCE
premium_projects.action: This project focuses on improving the productivity and sustainability of tea plantations through proper field maintenance practices and the application of organic manure. The investment includes activities such as plucking weeding soil conservation and the use of organic fertilizers (such as buying animal manure) to restore soil fertility. The project aims to enhance tea quality and yield while reducing dependence on chemical fertilizers and promoting environmentally friendly farming practices
premium_projects.challenge: The key challenges include declining soil fertility from continuous tea cultivation leading to reduced yields and lower green leaf quality. Farmers also face high fertilizer costs and limited access to inputs along with poor plantation management practices such as delayed pruning and inadequate weeding. In addition soil erosion limited knowledge of organic manure use and climate variability further negatively affect tea productivity.
premium_projects.intended_outcome: The project is expected to increase tea production and improve leaf quality while restoring soil fertility and ensuring the long-term sustainability of plantations. It will reduce production costs by lowering dependence on chemical fertilizers and promote better environmental conservation and soil protection. Overall it will enhance farmers’ incomes improve knowledge and adoption of sustainable farming practices and strengthen the resilience of tea plantations to climate change.

premium_projects.action: The project is an initiative that stems from the need identified in the needs assessment carried out by our committee in 2025, the idea is to install solar panels for the generation of electrical energy in homes that are owned by workers, helping to avoid environmental wear and tear by generating clean and renewable energy and providing appliances such as pots, heaters, air fryers, induction stoves, and others to gradually migrate to electrical energy from solar panels and eliminate the use of gas or wood burning appliances, thereby reducing the carbon footprint generated by all workers' homes within the scope of the certificate. The project will be funded 100% with the premium received by our committee.
premium_projects.challenge: The results of the needs assessment showed that our workers and their families cook using mainly LP gas and this represents an expense that seriously impacts their economy when, without warning, they run out of gas to continue cooking and have to buy it overnight. That is why there is a need for workers' homes to migrate and start using clean and renewable energies that do not cause pollution, seeking to make homes self-sustainable first by generating their own electricity and then equipping them with devices that work based on this electricity to meet the most basic needs such as electricity, hot water, cooking, etc.
premium_projects.intended_outcome: Install solar panels to generate electricity in workers' homes and provide them with stoves, ovens, electric heaters, etc. to make it a self-sustainable home. The beneficiaries will be the workers of Edulag and Pentágono Agrícola and their families, approximately 300 people between children and adults. The impact will be measured in updates to the needs assessment when the number of people who rely on gas and firewood in addition to paying for the electricity they consume is getting lower and lower. In addition, the Fair Trade Committee will carry out the following activities: President: to follow up on projects and organize the other members of the committee and assign specific tasks for the execution of the project. Treasurer: keep track of premium expenses in the project. Secretary: draw up minutes of each project follow-up meeting. Vocals: support the specific activities of the project that are assigned to them.
